decisions.quote: As a result of repeated exposure to the running IE component of the intervention, high AS participants, but not low AS participants, experienced a decrease in catastrophic cognitions about the sensations associated with running and a decrease in fear of these arousal sensations. This result is consistent with results from our previous process study (Sabourin et al., 2008). As expected, high AS participants also experienced decreases in somatic reactions to running over time. Contrary to predictions, however, the low AS group did not reveal a decline in somatic reactions to the running.
decisions.reason: In the original study (Sabourin et al., 2008), cognitive and affective reactions to running decreased in high AS but not low AS women, whereas somatic reactions decreased in both high and low AS women (Introduction, lines 220-225). The present replication tested all three reaction domains across high and low AS groups (lines 275-281, 526-556). While the cognitive and affective decreases (high AS only) and the high-AS somatic decrease replicated, the low-AS somatic decrease did not replicate, which the Discussion explicitly notes was contrary to predictions (lines 709-721). Because some tested findings from the original study replicated and one did not, the outcome is mixed.
